decided.claim: Demote by a handicapped save time, not an absolute tier: a session known to hold <=1 pane competes in rank() as though saved TRIVIAL_HANDICAP earlier (effective_saved), so substance beats a throwaway near-term while recency always wins eventually — the abandoned giant cannot squat forever.

Record substance as a top-level `panes = N` scalar in the state file, written by build_state beside last_workspace, so the adoption scan reads it with the existing hand-rolled top-level line scanner — no TOML deserialization added to the boot path, and one read_to_string per candidate now serves both hints.

A missing pane count (pre-upgrade files) is never docked: Candidate.panes = None reads as substantial, which is what keeps existing sessions ahead of fresh throwaways on the first launch after upgrading.

Trivial means exactly panes <= 1 (a two-pane session already counts as arranged), and TRIVIAL_HANDICAP is 72h — sized to cover arrange-on-Friday / quick-window-Monday-morning while bounding how long a stale big session can outrank live trivial work.
The workspace hint stays the untouched first sort key; the handicap only reshapes the recency comparison beneath it, so a session you were just standing on wins however small it is.

Refactored toml_top_level_string into a shared raw-value helper (toml_top_level_value) plus string/usize wrappers, rather than duplicating the stop-at-first-table line scanner for the new numeric key.

Pinned the writer/scanner contract with a test (adoption_hints_serialize_into_the_top_level_table): toml 0.8 must emit both hints above the first `[` table header, since the scanner stops there and struct field order alone does not guarantee it.
Left rank() shared between adoption and scratch-window theme borrowing (resolve_key/theme_key_in), so tear-offs inherit the same substance-aware order rather than forking a second ranking.

least_confident.why: Both numbers are judgment calls: a two-pane throwaway still wins by pure recency, and the Friday-evening-to-Monday-morning gap (~63h) only just fits inside 72h; a different team might pick a tier per pane count or a different window.

Any wrong winner refreshes its own mtime when adopted and closed, re-arming itself; that dynamic is pre-existing under pure recency, but the handicap extends the window in which a recently-closed big session can keep outranking new trivial work by up to 72h.

A scratch window torn off near a one-pane session may now borrow the look of an older bigger session within the handicap instead of its literal parent; cosmetic only, but I could not observe it against a running compositor.

not_done.claim: Nothing was compiled or executed: cargo build/test, all new and edited tests, and the toml 0.8 serializer behaviors the change leans on (scalar hoisting above tables, None-field omission) are unverified — asserted by the new test but never run.
not_done.why: Builds and test runs are out of scope for this exercise by instruction.

not_done.claim: No richer substance metric (tab count, agent panes, cwd variety) and no graded decay — pane count with a binary threshold only.
not_done.why: Proportionate to the ask; the scan must stay cheap and the story only requires demoting the one-pane throwaway.

not_done.claim: Adoption-time save behavior unchanged: a session adopted and immediately closed still refreshes its mtime and re-wins the next launch.
not_done.why: Pre-existing dynamic of mtime-based ranking, orthogonal to the ticket; changing save triggers has blast radius across the shrink guard and backups.

not_done.claim: share_demo's cloned state now also carries `panes`; behavior of demo windows under it is unverified.
not_done.why: Demo state is loaded from TD_DEMO_STATE outside the sessions directory and is never adopted, so it should be inert — but only a running app would confirm.
